LDSO-Deontic: Formal Deontic Norm Ontology

Abstract

LDSO-Deontic is an RDF/OWL vocabulary for formal, executable norms: rules with a strength (strict, defeasible, defeater), formal conditions, deontic conclusions (obligation, prohibition, permission, right) with bearers, actions, targets and deadlines, reparation chains, and explicit overrides with their legal basis. It covers the deontic and defeasible constructs of [[LEGALRULEML]] and of the [[ODRL]] Information Model, and compiles to the HydraDL defeasible deontic reasoner. It occupies Layer 5a of the Legal Document Structure Ontology (LDSO) stack, above [[LDSO-SEMANTICS]] and [[LDSO-OPERATIONS]].

Status notice: This document is not an official W3C Standard or W3C Recommendation. It is a community/project specification using W3C ReSpec formatting conventions.

This document is not an official W3C Standard or W3C Recommendation. It is a community/project specification produced by Geoknoesis LLC using W3C ReSpec formatting conventions. This is draft 0.1.0.

Ontology IRI: https://w3id.org/ldso/deontic — version IRI https://w3id.org/ldso/deontic/0.1.0 — preferred prefix deo:. Feedback is welcome via the GitHub issue tracker.

Overview

LDSO-Deontic is the vocabulary for formal, executable norms: rules with a strength (strict, defeasible, defeater), formal conditions, deontic conclusions (obligation, prohibition, permission, right) with bearers, actions, targets and deadlines, reparation chains, and explicit overrides with their legal basis. Norms also compute with values: predicates declare typed signatures (quantities and relations over numbers, instants, durations and texts), conditions compare, assign and aggregate values with exact arithmetic, rounding and calendar expressions, and an obligation may be over an amount ("pay at least the fee").

It covers the deontic and defeasible constructs of OASIS LegalRuleML Core 1.0 and of the W3C ODRL 2.2 Information Model, and it is designed so that a normative system expressed in it compiles to the defeasible deontic engine of HydraDL (hydradl-deontic).

Where it sits:

Layer Module Says
4 LDSO-Semantics (leg:) what a provision says: "Clause 8 states an obligation of the insurer"
5 LDSO-Operations (ops:) how it is operated: triggers, criteria, procedures, schedules
5a LDSO-Deontic (deo:) how it is formalised: O[insurer](paid(claim)) within 30 days of approval, ⊗ late fee; defeated by the flood exclusion

Two analysts can annotate a clause identically in leg: and still formalise it differently in deo: — hence a separate layer. deo:formalizes links each rule, condition or statement back to the annotation it formalises, so a reasoner's explanation can cite the source provision.

Usage Pattern

ex:r_pay
  a deo:PrescriptiveRule ;
  deo:strength deo:DefeasibleStrength ;
  deo:hasCondition ex:c_covered , ex:c_insurer_of , ex:c_approved ;
  deo:activatedBy ex:c_approved ;                       # the clock starts at approval
  deo:hasConsequent [
    a deo:ReparationChain ;
    deo:hasChainElement
      [ a deo:ChainElement ; deo:position 1 ; deo:statement ex:obl_pay ] ,      # pay within 30 days
      [ a deo:ChainElement ; deo:position 2 ; deo:statement ex:obl_late_fee ]   # else a late fee
  ] ;
  deo:formalizes ex:Oblig_Clause8 .                     # → leg:annotates → Clause 8

ex:ov_flood
  a deo:Override ;
  deo:overriding ex:r_flood_endorsement ;
  deo:overridden ex:r_flood_exclusion ;
  deo:overrideBasis deo:LexSpecialis ;
  deo:basisProvision ex:endorsement_3 .

A computed value: the late fee is 1.5% of the claim amount, to the cent, and the insurer must pay at least that fee.

ex:r_late_fee_amount
  a deo:ConstitutiveRule ;
  deo:strength deo:StrictStrength ;
  deo:hasCondition ex:c_claim_amount ,                  # claimAmount(?claim, ?amount)
                   [ a deo:AssignmentCondition ;         # ?fee = round(0.015 × ?amount, 2, half even)
                     deo:assigns ex:var_fee ;
                     deo:expression [
                       a deo:Expression ; deo:operation deo:Round ;
                       deo:places 2 ; deo:roundingMode deo:HalfEven ;
                       deo:hasOperand [ a deo:ExpressionOperand ; deo:position 1 ; deo:operandValue [
                         a deo:Expression ; deo:operation deo:Mul ;
                         deo:hasOperand [ a deo:ExpressionOperand ; deo:position 1 ; deo:operandValue 0.015 ] ,
                                        [ a deo:ExpressionOperand ; deo:position 2 ; deo:operandValue ex:var_amount ] ] ] ] ] ;
  deo:concludes ex:lit_late_fee_amount .                # lateFeeAmount(?claim, ?fee)

ex:obl_late_fee
  a deo:Obligation ;
  deo:bearer ex:var_insurer ;
  deo:action ex:act_pay_late_fee ;                      # paidLateFee(?claim, ?fee)
  deo:fulfilmentComparator ops:GreaterThanOrEqual .     # a payment ≥ the fee fulfils it

claimAmount and lateFeeAmount are declared quantities (one value per claim) and paidLateFee a relation (any number of payments), each with a deo:PredicateSignature on the normative system.

Modelling rules the shapes enforce:

  • Priority is never implicit: every deo:Override records its basis, and overrides form no cycle.
  • Reparation chains are ordered by deo:position (LDSO never uses rdf:List); only the last element may be a permission.
  • A record is open unless the system declares it complete (deo:declaresComplete): without that, a missing payment record never proves a payment was not made.
  • Variables are scoped to their rule, and (in the HydraDL profile) every variable must be bound by a positive fact, class or property condition, or by an assignment or aggregate, whose variable is fresh.
  • Signatures are well formed: argument slots indexed 0..n-1, a key no longer than the arguments, and exactly one value after the key for a quantity; one signature per predicate.
  • Expressions have operands at positions 1..n, as many as their operation takes; deo:Round and only it has deo:places and deo:roundingMode; an expression never contains itself.
  • Sets are repeated values, not lists: deo:IsAnyOf and deo:IsNoneOf take one deo:rightOperand per member, every other operator exactly one.

Coverage: LegalRuleML Core 1.0

LegalRuleML is XML-first; terms are its element and attribute names. Its deontic sub-kinds and legal statuses are not elements: documents name them by @iri, and LDSO-Deontic gives them concepts.

LegalRuleML LDSO-Deontic

ConstitutiveStatement deo:ConstitutiveRule (shape: no deontic consequent)
FactualStatement deo:FactualStatement + deo:asserts
ruleml:Rule if / then deo:hasCondition / deo:hasConsequent or deo:concludes
ruleml:Neg deo:negated true
ruleml:Naf no per-condition operator: declare the predicate complete (deo:declaresComplete), so absence counts as false
ruleml:Var, ruleml:Ind, ruleml:Atom deo:Variable, individual IRIs, deo:Literal + deo:Argument
ruleml:Data (typed values), ruleml:Expr + ruleml:Fun (built-in functions) typed literals; deo:Expression with deo:operation and ordered deo:ExpressionOperand nodes
(none: predicate typing) deo:PredicateSignature, deo:declaresSignature

StrictStrength, DefeasibleStrength, Defeater deo:StrictStrength, deo:DefeasibleStrength, deo:DefeaterStrength
Obligation, Prohibition, Permission, Right deo:Obligation, deo:Prohibition, deo:Permission, deo:Right

Bearer, AuxiliaryParty deo:bearer, deo:auxiliaryParty (+ deo:beneficiary)

SuborderList (⊗) deo:ReparationChain, deo:ChainElement, deo:position (its last element may be a permission)

toPrescriptiveStatement, appliesPenalty deo:repairs, deo:imposes
PenaltyStatement, Penalty deo:reparationKind deo:Penalty, deo:imposes
Violation, Compliance (as premises) deo:NormCondition with deo:Violated / deo:Fulfilled (both executable)

(none: priority's justification) deo:overrideBasis, deo:basisProvision

TemporalCharacteristic, hasTemporalCharacteristic deo:TemporalCharacteristic, deo:temporalCharacteristic
forStatus, hasStatusDevelopment, atTime deo:forStatus, deo:statusDevelopment, deo:atTime

Authority, Jurisdiction, LegalSource (+ collections) deo:authority, deo:jurisdiction, deo:legalSource (repeat the property)
Paraphrase deo:paraphrase
Comment rdfs:comment
Agent, Figure, Role ent:NamedEntity with ent:entityType ent:Role (LDSO-Entities), as bearer / auxiliary party

Context, Association, appliesAssociation, appliesSource… not reified: the metadata goes on the rule itself (deo:legalSource, deo:authority, deo:jurisdiction, deo:temporalCharacteristic), and deo:formalizes links the rule to its annotation

Compiling to HydraDL

Data that conforms to shapes.ttl and hydradl-profile-shapes.ttl compiles to a hydradl_deontic::NormSystem that passes NormSystem::validate(). The compiler still calls validate(), which also catches violation cycles through Violated conditions (beyond SPARQL's reach).

LDSO-Deontic hydradl-deontic
deo:NormativeSystem NormSystem
deo:hasRule (with deo:inheritsFrom*) NormSystem.rules (the union)
deo:Override NormSystem.superiority pair (overriding, overridden)
deo:declaresComplete NormSystem.closed (fact predicates, named classes, roles)
deo:Rule IRI, deo:formalizes → citation Rule.id, Rule.source
deo:strength RuleKind::Strict / Defeasible / Defeater
deo:hasCondition Rule.body
deo:activatedBy Rule.activated_by (index of that condition)
deo:FactCondition Condition::Fact(Literal)
deo:ClassCondition Condition::Class { class, term, positive }
deo:PropertyCondition Condition::Role { role, subject, object, positive }
deo:NormCondition deo:InForce / deo:Violated / deo:Fulfilled Condition::InForce / Condition::Violated / Condition::Fulfilled
deo:declaresSignature → deo:PredicateSignature NormSystem.signatures: Signature { args, key, quantity } from the slots' deo:valueType in deo:argumentIndex order, deo:keyLength and deo:isQuantity
deo:ValueTypeScheme concepts ValueType::Individual / Number / Instant / Duration / Text
deo:utcOffset NormSystem.utc_offset (seconds; absent: 0)
deo:Expression + deo:operation + operands in deo:position order Expr::… (deo:Mul → Expr::Mul, deo:Lesser / deo:Greater → Expr::Min / Max, deo:Round → Expr::Round(e, deo:places, Rounding))
deo:operandValue / deo:expression a literal, an individual, a variable Expr::Term(Term::Value(…)) (xsd:decimal/integer → Number, xsd:dateTime → Instant, xsd:duration → Duration, xsd:string → Text) / Term::Individual / Term::Variable
deo:AssignmentCondition Condition::Let { var: deo:assigns, expr: deo:expression }
deo:AggregateCondition Condition::Aggregate { var, op: deo:aggregateOperator (Sum / Count / Min / Max), expr, pattern: deo:pattern }
deo:ConstitutiveRule concluding a literal whose value argument is an assigned variable Head::Fact of a computed value (a quantity competes with other values of its key)
deo:ComparisonCondition with an ops:Comparator Condition::Fact(leftOperand(key, ?v)) + Condition::Compare { left: ?v, op, right: rightOperand }
deo:ComparisonCondition with deo:IsAnyOf / deo:IsNoneOf that fact condition + Condition::In { expr: ?v, values: every deo:rightOperand, positive: true / false }
deo:ComparisonCondition with deo:IsA that fact condition + Condition::Class { class: rightOperand, term: ?v }
ops:Equal, ops:NotEqual, ops:LessThan, ops:LessThanOrEqual, ops:GreaterThan, ops:GreaterThanOrEqual Cmp::Eq, Ne, Lt, Le, Gt, Ge
deo:fulfilmentComparator Deontic::fulfilled_when(Cmp) (absent: Cmp::Eq)
deo:PrescriptiveRule + one statement Head::Norm(Deontic)
deo:PrescriptiveRule + deo:ReparationChain Head::Chain(Vec<Deontic>) in deo:position order; the last element may be permitted
deo:ConstitutiveRule Head::Fact(Literal)
deo:FactualStatement a strict rule with an empty body and Head::Fact
deo:Obligation / deo:Prohibition / deo:Permission Deontic::obliged / forbidden (= obliged of the negated action) / permitted
deo:bearer Deontic.bearer (a Term)
deo:action (+ deo:target as a trailing argument when the action does not name it) Deontic.action
deo:deadline → ops:deadlineDuration Deadline::Within(seconds)
deo:deadline → ops:deadlineDate Deadline::At(timestamp)
deo:Variable / individual IRI Term::Variable / Term::Individual

Constructs the compiler rewrites (no HydraDL counterpart needed):

Construct Compiled as
deo:Right the bearer's permission plus each deo:correlative statement, all concluded by the same rule body
deo:Reparation the imposed statement appended to the chain of every rule concluding the repaired statement (the profile requires it to be that chain's last element; one imposing a permission must be the statement's only reparation, so the permission ends the chain)
deo:requiresDuty a rule with the permission's conditions concluding the duty, and Condition::Fulfilled { duty } added to the permission's rule
the key of a deo:ComparisonCondition the target of the refined statement (whose action or target collection the comparison refines), else the subject of the rule's only positive class condition; with neither, or with positive class conditions on several subjects, the profile reports that the compiler cannot place the key
deo:LogicalCondition And / Or / Xone inlined conjunction / one rule per operand / one rule per operand with the others negated (disjunctive normal form, nested operands expanded)
deo:refinement added to the conditions of each rule using the refined action or collection
deo:AssetCollection / deo:PartyCollection as target / bearer a fresh variable with a deo:memberOf fact condition
deo:includedIn strict constitutive rules: doing the narrower act is doing the broader one
deo:implies a defeater against prohibitions of the implied act when the implying act is permitted
deo:conflictStrategy deo:PermissionPrevails / ProhibitionPrevails overrides (basis deo:ConflictStrategyBasis) of each permission rule over each contrary prohibition rule, or the reverse
deo:conflictStrategy deo:Invalidate ambiguity blocking; any reported Conflict makes the whole system void
deo:policyType deo:Offer / deo:Request nothing in force (the profile warns)
deo:Alternatives the adopted alternative; with none adopted, one NormSystem per alternative

Time. HydraDL counts time in i64 seconds. A duration compiles to its length in seconds, which is only defined for weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds (G8). A date compiles to a timestamp; the proposed convention is the end of that day at the system's deo:utcOffset (UTC when absent) — this is an open choice for the compiler, recorded here so it is made once. The calendar operations (deo:YearsBetween, deo:AddMonths…) count civil dates at the same offset, so an age or a date "six months after filing" can be computed and compared, even though a deadline cannot yet be stated in months (G8).

Values. Numbers are exact rationals: 0.015 × 1234.56 is exactly 18.5184, and only deo:Round, deo:Floor and deo:Ceil round. A missing value of an open recorded predicate is unknown, and so is whatever is computed from it (an obligation over it has status Unknown, never NotApplicable). Aggregates have set semantics: records that must count separately carry an identifying argument (wage(?person, ?month, ?amount)). See the hydradl-deontic README, "Values".

Gaps: valid LDSO-Deontic that HydraDL does not yet execute

Each is a Violation of hydradl-profile-shapes.ttl; examples/licence.ttl has one instance of each, and the test suite checks that exactly these seven are reported. The numbering is kept stable: G1 (fulfilled conditions and ODRL duty preconditions) and G6 (a permission ending a reparation chain) are closed, and G4 is narrowed from every comparison to the part-of and set operands.

Gap Construct Source What it needs in the engine
G2 deo:temporalCharacteristic (rule validity windows) LegalRuleML TemporalCharacteristic a validity interval per rule, checked against the evaluation time
G3 maintenance and punctual obligations; preemptive and perdurant ones LegalRuleML deontic @iri kinds status rules per obligation type
G4 (part-of and set operands) deo:IsPartOf, deo:HasPart, deo:IsAllOf; deo:rightOperandReference; deo:status ODRL isPartOf, hasPart, isAllOf, rightOperandReference, status containment between individuals (a spatial or mereological relation), sets as values, right operands looked up at evaluation time, and status values generated from the exercised action
G5 deo:AndSequence ODRL andSequence order in time between condition facts
G7 recurring and period schedules LDSO-Operations schedules one obligation instance per period
G8 calendar durations (months, years) as deadlines legal text ("within six months") a deadline computed with calendar arithmetic from the activation date
G9 deo:deonticContent (a norm about a norm) LegalRuleML recursive deontics nested modalities

Until G4 is closed, record a part-of comparison's outcome as a fact (inEU(?dataset)) and use a deo:FactCondition. Comparisons with stated values — =, ≠, <, ≤, >, ≥, deo:IsAnyOf, deo:IsNoneOf and deo:IsA — are executable.

Statuses

HydraDL reports, for each obligation instance, one of NotApplicable, Active, Fulfilled, Violated or Unknown (the last when an open record leaves it undecided). The standards' state terms read off these:

Standard term HydraDL result
LegalRuleML Violation; ODRL infringed (prohibition), duty not fulfilled Status::Violated
LegalRuleML Compliance; ODRL fulfilled Status::Fulfilled
ODRL satisfied (constraint) the condition is proved (+∂)
ODRL exercised (permission) a fact of the permitted action is recorded
ODRL void (policy, under invalid) some Conflict is reported
strong permission / weak permission +∂ P concluded / no prohibition concluded

Open Questions

  1. Date convention — which instant ops:deadlineDate denotes. The time zone is now stated per system (deo:utcOffset); proposed: the end of that day at that offset.
  2. Strict deontic rules — HydraDL lets a superior rule beat a strict deontic rule (only factual conclusions have a strict tier). LegalRuleML leaves this open; documented on deo:StrictStrength.
  3. Root README — the LDSO layer table should gain a row for Layer 5a (LDSO-Deontic) once this module is accepted.

Class Reference

deo:Action

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Action
LabelAction
Subclass ofdeo:Literal
DefinitionWhat a deontic statement requires, forbids or permits the bearer to do: a literal whose predicate is the act (pay, notify, use, print) and whose arguments are what it is done to.
UsageODRL Action (the value of odrl:action) together with the statement's target; the act's type is the deo:predicate (an ODRL action IRI or a domain act). A negated action reads "refrain from". Narrowing an action (odrl:refinement) is done with deo:refinement. Relations between act types (odrl:includedIn, odrl:implies) are stated on the act-type IRIs with deo:includedIn and deo:implies.
ex:act_pay
  a deo:Action ;
  deo:predicate ex:payClaim ;
  deo:hasArgument [ a deo:Argument ; deo:argumentIndex 0 ; deo:argumentValue ex:var_claim ] .

deo:AggregateCondition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#AggregateCondition
LabelAggregate Condition
Subclass ofdeo:Condition
DefinitionA condition that binds a fresh variable to the sum, count, minimum or maximum of an expression over every distinct solution of a pattern of conditions: "?gross is the sum of ?amount over wage(?person, ?month, ?amount)".
UsageThe operator is deo:aggregateOperator, the bound variable deo:assigns, the value of each solution deo:expression, and the pattern deo:pattern (fact, class and property conditions). A variable of the pattern also bound elsewhere in the rule is a group key; the others are local to the aggregate. Set semantics: each distinct solution counts once, so records that must count separately carry an identifying argument (the month of a wage). Over no solution a sum or count is 0 and a minimum or maximum has no value (the condition is refuted); over an open base predicate the aggregate is undetermined. Never negated. HydraDL: Condition::Aggregate { var, op, expr, pattern }.
ex:c_gross
  a deo:AggregateCondition ;
  deo:aggregateOperator deo:Sum ;
  deo:assigns ex:var_gross ;
  deo:expression ex:var_wage ;
  deo:pattern [
    a deo:FactCondition ;
    deo:predicate ex:wage ;
    deo:hasArgument [ a deo:Argument ; deo:argumentIndex 0 ; deo:argumentValue ex:var_person ] ,
                    [ a deo:Argument ; deo:argumentIndex 1 ; deo:argumentValue ex:var_month ] ,
                    [ a deo:Argument ; deo:argumentIndex 2 ; deo:argumentValue ex:var_wage ]
  ] .

deo:Alternatives

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Alternatives
LabelAlternatives
Subclass of—
DefinitionA set of mutually exclusive formalisations of the same provision: competing interpretations, of which at most one is adopted at a time.
UsageLegalRuleML Alternatives (hasAlternative, fromLegalSources). Each alternative (deo:alternative) is a rule. An evaluation uses the one named by deo:adopted, or evaluates each alternative separately and reports per interpretation.
ex:alt_art7
  a deo:Alternatives ;
  deo:alternative ex:r_art7_strict_reading , ex:r_art7_broad_reading ;
  deo:adopted ex:r_art7_strict_reading .

deo:Argument

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Argument
LabelArgument
Subclass of—
DefinitionOne argument of a literal: its position and its value.
UsageIndexes start at 0 and are consecutive within a literal.
ex:arg_0
  a deo:Argument ;
  deo:argumentIndex 0 ;
  deo:argumentValue ex:var_claim .

deo:ArgumentSlot

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#ArgumentSlot
LabelArgument Slot
Subclass of—
DefinitionOne argument position of a predicate signature and the type of value it holds.
UsageIndexes start at 0 and are consecutive within a signature. The type is a concept of deo:ValueTypeScheme.
ex:slot_amount
  a deo:ArgumentSlot ;
  deo:argumentIndex 1 ;
  deo:valueType deo:Number .

deo:AssetCollection

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#AssetCollection
LabelAsset Collection
Subclass ofdeo:Collection
DefinitionA collection of the things actions are performed on.
UsageODRL AssetCollection.
ex:all_claims_2026 a deo:AssetCollection .

deo:AssignmentCondition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#AssignmentCondition
LabelAssignment Condition
Subclass ofdeo:Condition
DefinitionA condition that binds a fresh variable to a computed value: "let ?fee be round(0.015 × ?amount, 2)".
UsageThe variable is given by deo:assigns and the value by deo:expression (a deo:Expression, a deo:Variable or a literal). It holds once the expression's variables are bound; over an unknown value the assigned value is unknown. The variable must be bound nowhere else in the rule. A constitutive rule concluding a literal whose value argument is the assigned variable computes a value of that predicate. Never negated. HydraDL: Condition::Let { var, expr }.
ex:c_fee
  a deo:AssignmentCondition ;
  deo:assigns ex:var_fee ;
  deo:expression ex:expr_fee .

deo:ChainElement

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#ChainElement
LabelChain Element
Subclass of—
DefinitionOne position of a reparation chain and the deontic statement at that position.
UsagePositions start at 1 and are consecutive within a chain.
ex:chain_pay_1
  a deo:ChainElement ;
  deo:position 1 ;
  deo:statement ex:obl_pay .

deo:ClassCondition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#ClassCondition
LabelClass Condition
Subclass ofdeo:Condition
DefinitionA condition that an individual belongs (or, if negated, does not belong) to an OWL class, decided by a DL reasoner over the ontology.
UsageThe class is named by deo:classExpression (a named class, or a class expression node); the individual by deo:subject. Answered one-way: an entailment establishes it, an entailed complement refutes it, anything else leaves it undetermined unless the class is declared complete. HydraDL: Condition::Class.
ex:c_flood
  a deo:ClassCondition ;
  deo:classExpression ex:FloodClaim ;
  deo:subject ex:var_claim .

deo:Collection

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Collection
LabelCollection
Subclass of—
DefinitionA set of assets or parties a rule refers to as a whole, optionally narrowed by refinements.
UsageODRL AssetCollection and PartyCollection. Members point to it with deo:memberOf (odrl:partOf). A rule over a collection applies to each member that satisfies its refinements: a compiler turns it into a variable with a membership condition.
ex:all_claims_2026
  a deo:AssetCollection ;
  deo:refinement ex:c_filed_in_2026 .

deo:ComparisonCondition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#ComparisonCondition
LabelComparison Condition
Subclass ofdeo:Condition
DefinitionA condition comparing a measured or stated value (the left operand) with a value (the right operand) by an operator, such as count ≤ 5, dateTime < 2027-01-01, or spatial isPartOf EU.
UsageODRL Constraint (leftOperand, operator, rightOperand, rightOperandReference, unit, dataType, status). Order comparisons reuse the LDSO-Operations comparators (ops:Comparator); set and part operators use the deo:SetOperator individuals. The left operand is a predicate with a value (a quantity such as ex:claimedAmount, or an ODRL left operand); its key is the target of the statement the condition refines, or else the subject of the rule's only positive class condition. HydraDL: a fact condition binding the left operand's value, then Condition::Compare (for a comparator), Condition::In (deo:IsAnyOf, deo:IsNoneOf, with one deo:rightOperand per member) or Condition::Class (deo:IsA, the right operand a class). Part-of and all-of operators, right operands looked up through deo:rightOperandReference, and comparisons of an ODRL status (deo:status) are not executable.
ex:c_amount_cap
  a deo:ComparisonCondition ;
  deo:leftOperand ex:claimedAmount ;
  deo:operator ops:LessThanOrEqual ;
  deo:rightOperand "10000"^^xsd:decimal ;
  deo:unit "USD" .

deo:Condition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Condition
LabelCondition
Subclass of—
DefinitionOne conjunct of a rule's antecedent: something that must hold in a situation for the rule to apply.
UsageAbstract: use deo:FactCondition, deo:ClassCondition, deo:PropertyCondition, deo:NormCondition, deo:ComparisonCondition, deo:LogicalCondition, deo:AssignmentCondition or deo:AggregateCondition. A condition is evaluated with three values: established, refuted, or undetermined (when the record is open and silent). The formal counterpart of an LDSO-Semantics leg:Condition or leg:Exception (link with deo:formalizes) and of an ODRL Constraint or LogicalConstraint.
ex:c_payable
  a deo:ClassCondition ;
  deo:classExpression ex:PayableClaim ;
  deo:subject ex:var_claim .

deo:ConstitutiveRule

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#ConstitutiveRule
LabelConstitutive Rule
Subclass ofdeo:Rule
DefinitionA rule whose conclusion establishes an institutional fact or a classification ("X counts as Y in context C") rather than prescribing behaviour.
UsageLegalRuleML ConstitutiveStatement: its conclusion must not be a deontic formula. The conclusion is a deo:Literal given by deo:concludes. Definitions that are plain class axioms belong in OWL (and are reasoned with by a DL reasoner); use a constitutive rule when the conclusion depends on facts of a case or must be defeasible.
ex:r_late_payment
  a deo:ConstitutiveRule ;
  deo:strength deo:StrictStrength ;
  deo:hasCondition ex:c_paid_after_deadline ;
  deo:concludes ex:lit_late_payment .

deo:DeonticStatement

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#DeonticStatement
LabelDeontic Statement
Subclass of—
DefinitionThe conclusion of a prescriptive rule: that a bearer must, must not, or may perform an action, possibly on a target, possibly by a deadline.
UsageAbstract: use deo:Obligation, deo:Prohibition, deo:Permission or deo:Right. The bearer (deo:bearer) is the party the statement is primarily directed at (LegalRuleML Bearer; ODRL assignee); other parties are deo:auxiliaryParty (LegalRuleML AuxiliaryParty; ODRL assigner). The same deontic statement may be the conclusion of several rules: rules that conclude the same statement compete over its parameters (for example its deadline), and an override decides which applies.
ex:obl_pay
  a deo:Obligation ;
  deo:bearer ex:insurer_role ;
  deo:action ex:act_pay ;
  deo:deadline ex:dl_30_days .

deo:Expression

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Expression
LabelExpression
Subclass of—
DefinitionA computation over values: an operation applied to ordered operands, such as 0.015 × ?amount, round(?x, 2) or the whole years between two instants.
UsageThe operation is a concept of deo:OperationScheme (deo:operation). Operands are deo:ExpressionOperand nodes ordered by deo:position (LDSO never uses rdf:List); each operand's value is a literal, an individual, a deo:Variable or a nested expression. deo:Round also takes deo:places and deo:roundingMode. Arithmetic is exact. Used by deo:AssignmentCondition and deo:AggregateCondition. HydraDL: Expr.
ex:expr_fee
  a deo:Expression ;
  deo:operation deo:Round ;
  deo:places 2 ;
  deo:roundingMode deo:HalfEven ;
  deo:hasOperand [ a deo:ExpressionOperand ; deo:position 1 ; deo:operandValue [
    a deo:Expression ;
    deo:operation deo:Mul ;
    deo:hasOperand [ a deo:ExpressionOperand ; deo:position 1 ; deo:operandValue "0.015"^^xsd:decimal ] ,
                   [ a deo:ExpressionOperand ; deo:position 2 ; deo:operandValue ex:var_amount ]
  ] ] .

deo:ExpressionOperand

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#ExpressionOperand
LabelExpression Operand
Subclass of—
DefinitionOne operand of an expression: its position and its value.
UsagePositions start at 1 and are consecutive within an expression; the order matters for subtraction, division and the calendar operations.
ex:operand_rate
  a deo:ExpressionOperand ;
  deo:position 1 ;
  deo:operandValue "0.015"^^xsd:decimal .

deo:FactCondition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#FactCondition
LabelFact Condition
Subclass ofdeo:Condition, deo:Literal
DefinitionA condition that a literal holds in the situation — a recorded fact, possibly with a time — or, if negated, that it does not.
UsageWhether an unrecorded fact counts as false depends on whether its predicate is declared complete (deo:declaresComplete). HydraDL: Condition::Fact. The time of the fact a rule is activated by sets when its obligation starts (deo:activatedBy).
ex:c_approved_at
  a deo:FactCondition ;
  deo:predicate ex:approvedAt ;
  deo:hasArgument [ a deo:Argument ; deo:argumentIndex 0 ; deo:argumentValue ex:var_claim ] .

deo:FactualStatement

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#FactualStatement
LabelFactual Statement
Subclass of—
DefinitionA statement of fact made by the normative system itself, without conditions — for example that a named body is the competent authority.
UsageLegalRuleML FactualStatement. The fact is a deo:Literal given by deo:asserts. A reasoner treats it as a fact of every situation the system is evaluated in.
ex:fs_authority
  a deo:FactualStatement ;
  deo:asserts ex:lit_agency_competent .

deo:Literal

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Literal
LabelLiteral
Subclass of—
DefinitionAn atomic formula, possibly negated: a predicate applied to ordered arguments, such as paid(?claim) or ¬disclosed(?record).
UsageThe building block of conditions, actions and factual conclusions. The predicate (deo:predicate) is an IRI — a domain predicate, an ODRL action, an LDSO-Entities concept. Arguments (deo:hasArgument) are deo:Argument nodes ordered by deo:argumentIndex; their values are named entities or deo:Variable nodes. A predicate whose arguments include values (numbers, instants, durations, texts) declares a deo:PredicateSignature; a value argument is then a variable, bound by a fact or computed by a deo:AssignmentCondition. HydraDL: Literal { atom, positive }.
ex:lit_paid
  a deo:Literal ;
  deo:predicate ex:paid ;
  deo:hasArgument [ a deo:Argument ; deo:argumentIndex 0 ; deo:argumentValue ex:var_claim ] .

deo:LogicalCondition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#LogicalCondition
LabelLogical Condition
Subclass ofdeo:Condition
DefinitionA condition combining other conditions with a logical operator: and, or, exclusive or, or and-in-sequence.
UsageODRL LogicalConstraint (and, or, xone, andSequence). Operands are given by deo:operand; for and-in-sequence, by deo:SequencedOperand nodes with a deo:position. A compiler maps and to a conjunction, or to one rule per operand, and exclusive-or to one rule per operand with the others negated; and-in-sequence (order in time) is not yet executable by HydraDL.
ex:c_either
  a deo:LogicalCondition ;
  deo:logicalOperator deo:Or ;
  deo:operand ex:c_flood , ex:c_storm .

deo:NormativeSystem

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#NormativeSystem
LabelNormative System
Subclass of—
DefinitionA set of formal rules, overrides and factual statements that are evaluated together: a contract, a policy, a statute or part of one, as formalised. The unit a reasoner evaluates.
UsageCorresponds to an ODRL Policy (odrl:Policy and its subclasses, the policy type given by deo:policyType), to a LegalRuleML Statements collection or LegalRuleMLDocument, and to a HydraDL NormSystem. Rules belong to a normative system through deo:hasRule; overrides through deo:hasOverride. A normative system that inherits from another (odrl:inheritFrom) includes its rules. Predicates that carry values declare their signature (deo:declaresSignature); calendar functions use the system's deo:utcOffset.
ex:policy_2026
  a deo:NormativeSystem ;
  rdfs:label "Household insurance policy 2026, formalised"@en ;
  deo:policyType deo:Agreement ;
  deo:conflictStrategy deo:AmbiguityBlocking ;
  deo:legalSource ex:policy_doc ;
  deo:hasRule ex:r_pay_claim , ex:r_flood_endorsement ;
  deo:hasOverride ex:ov_flood .

deo:NormCondition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#NormCondition
LabelNorm Condition
Subclass ofdeo:Condition
DefinitionA condition on the normative state of a deontic statement: that it is in force, violated, or complied with.
UsageThe statement is given by deo:aboutStatement and the state by deo:normState (deo:InForce, deo:Violated, deo:Fulfilled). LegalRuleML Violation and Compliance used as premises. HydraDL: Condition::InForce, Condition::Violated and Condition::Fulfilled.
ex:c_pay_violated
  a deo:NormCondition ;
  deo:aboutStatement ex:obl_pay ;
  deo:normState deo:Violated .

deo:Obligation

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Obligation
LabelObligation
Subclass ofdeo:DeonticStatement
DefinitionThe bearer must perform the action (bring about the state). Failing to do so, by the deadline if any, is a violation.
UsageLegalRuleML Obligation; ODRL Duty (and policy-level odrl:obligation). The kind of obligation — achievement, maintenance or punctual — is given by deo:obligationType; preemption and perdurance by deo:preemptive and deo:perdurant. HydraDL: O[bearer](action).
ex:obl_notify
  a deo:Obligation ;
  deo:bearer ex:insurer_role ;
  deo:action ex:act_notify ;
  deo:obligationType deo:Achievement ;
  deo:deadline ex:dl_15_days .

deo:Override

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Override
LabelOverride
Subclass of—
DefinitionA stated priority between two rules: when both apply and conclude contrary things (or set different parameters of the same statement), the overriding rule prevails over the overridden one.
UsageLegalRuleML Override (@over, @under) and OverrideStatement; HydraDL superiority. Every override records its basis (deo:overrideBasis) — lex specialis, lex posterior, lex superior, an explicit clause, or the policy's conflict strategy — and may cite the provision that states it (deo:basisProvision). Priority is never inferred from the order rules appear in. Overrides must form no cycle.
ex:ov_flood
  a deo:Override ;
  deo:overriding ex:r_flood_endorsement ;
  deo:overridden ex:r_pay_claim ;
  deo:overrideBasis deo:LexSpecialis ;
  deo:basisProvision ex:endorsement_3 .

deo:PartyCollection

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#PartyCollection
LabelParty Collection
Subclass ofdeo:Collection
DefinitionA collection of parties a statement is borne by or addressed to.
UsageODRL PartyCollection.
ex:all_policyholders a deo:PartyCollection .

deo:Permission

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Permission
LabelPermission
Subclass ofdeo:DeonticStatement
DefinitionThe bearer may perform the action: an explicit (strong) permission, which can serve as an exception to a prohibition.
UsageLegalRuleML Permission; ODRL Permission. A permission stated by a rule is a strong permission. A weak permission ("not forbidden") is never stated: it is a conclusion of evaluation when no prohibition applies. ODRL duties that must be fulfilled before the permission can be exercised are attached with deo:requiresDuty. HydraDL: P[bearer](action). A permission may close a reparation chain: it then holds once every earlier element is violated.
ex:perm_request_docs
  a deo:Permission ;
  deo:bearer ex:insurer_role ;
  deo:action ex:act_request_documents .

deo:PredicateSignature

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#PredicateSignature
LabelPredicate Signature
Subclass of—
DefinitionThe argument types of a predicate that carries values (numbers, instants, durations, texts), which leading arguments identify a record (its key), and whether it is a quantity, with one value per key, or a relation, with any number.
UsageDeclared on the normative system with deo:declaresSignature. The arguments are deo:ArgumentSlot nodes ordered by deo:argumentIndex (LDSO never uses rdf:List). A quantity (deo:isQuantity true) has exactly one argument after its key: income(?person, ?amount). Its values compete: a recorded value beats a concluded one, the latest record wins, and rules concluding different values attack each other. A relation (deo:isQuantity false) may hold several values per key, such as payments. A predicate without a signature takes individuals only. HydraDL: NormSystem.signatures, Signature { args, key, quantity }.
ex:sig_claim_amount
  a deo:PredicateSignature ;
  deo:signaturePredicate ex:claimAmount ;
  deo:keyLength 1 ;
  deo:isQuantity true ;
  deo:hasArgumentSlot [ a deo:ArgumentSlot ; deo:argumentIndex 0 ; deo:valueType deo:Individual ] ,
                      [ a deo:ArgumentSlot ; deo:argumentIndex 1 ; deo:valueType deo:Number ] .

deo:PrescriptiveRule

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#PrescriptiveRule
LabelPrescriptive Rule
Subclass ofdeo:Rule
DefinitionA rule whose conclusion prescribes behaviour: a deontic statement, or a reparation chain of deontic statements.
UsageLegalRuleML PrescriptiveStatement; ODRL Permission, Prohibition and Duty. The conclusion is given by deo:hasConsequent.
ex:r_no_disclosure
  a deo:PrescriptiveRule ;
  deo:strength deo:StrictStrength ;
  deo:hasConsequent ex:proh_disclose .

deo:Prohibition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Prohibition
LabelProhibition
Subclass ofdeo:DeonticStatement
DefinitionThe bearer must not perform the action. Performing it is a violation (an infringement).
UsageLegalRuleML Prohibition; ODRL Prohibition. Equivalent to an obligation of the negated action; kept as its own class because both standards and legal text distinguish it. HydraDL: F[bearer](action) = O[bearer](¬action).
ex:proh_disclose
  a deo:Prohibition ;
  deo:bearer ex:insurer_role ;
  deo:action ex:act_disclose_records .

deo:PropertyCondition

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#PropertyCondition
LabelProperty Condition
Subclass ofdeo:Condition
DefinitionA condition that two individuals stand (or, if negated, do not stand) in an OWL object property, decided by a DL reasoner over the ontology.
UsageHydraDL: Condition::Role.
ex:c_insurer_of
  a deo:PropertyCondition ;
  deo:property ex:insurerOf ;
  deo:subject ex:var_insurer ;
  deo:object ex:var_claim .

deo:Reparation

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Reparation
LabelReparation
Subclass of—
DefinitionA stated link between a deontic statement and what its violation imposes: a consequence of a failed duty, a remedy for an infringed prohibition, or a penalty.
UsageLegalRuleML Reparation (appliesPenalty / toPrescriptiveStatement) and PenaltyStatement; ODRL consequence (on a Duty) and remedy (on a Prohibition). Use it when the reparation is stated separately from the primary norm (another clause, another rule); use deo:ReparationChain when one rule states the whole sequence. Both compile to the same HydraDL ⊗ chain: [repaired, imposed]. The kind is given by deo:reparationKind.
ex:rep_late_fee
  a deo:Reparation ;
  deo:repairs ex:obl_pay ;
  deo:imposes ex:obl_late_fee ;
  deo:reparationKind deo:Penalty .

deo:ReparationChain

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#ReparationChain
LabelReparation Chain
Subclass of—
DefinitionAn ordered sequence of deontic statements where each element after the first applies only once every earlier element has been violated: "do A; if A is violated, do B; if B is violated, do C".
UsageLegalRuleML SuborderList (the ⊗ operator of defeasible deontic logic); HydraDL Head::Chain. Members are deo:ChainElement nodes with an explicit deo:position (LDSO never uses rdf:List). A permission may only be the last element, since permissions cannot be violated. The first element's violation stays on record when the next element applies.
ex:chain_pay
  a deo:ReparationChain ;
  deo:hasChainElement [ a deo:ChainElement ; deo:position 1 ; deo:statement ex:obl_pay ] ,
                      [ a deo:ChainElement ; deo:position 2 ; deo:statement ex:obl_late_fee ] .

deo:Right

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Right
LabelRight
Subclass ofdeo:DeonticStatement
DefinitionA permission of the bearer together with the obligations or prohibitions it implies for auxiliary parties so that the bearer can exercise it (a claim-right in Hohfeld's sense).
UsageLegalRuleML Right. The correlative duties are listed with deo:correlative; each is an ordinary deontic statement borne by an auxiliary party. HydraDL has no right operator: a right compiles to the bearer's permission plus each correlative statement.
ex:right_access
  a deo:Right ;
  deo:bearer ex:policyholder_role ;
  deo:auxiliaryParty ex:insurer_role ;
  deo:action ex:act_access_file ;
  deo:correlative ex:obl_provide_file .

deo:Rule

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Rule
LabelRule
Subclass of—
DefinitionA formal rule: a conjunction of conditions (its antecedent) and a conclusion, with a strength saying how the conclusion resists contrary rules.
UsageAbstract: use deo:PrescriptiveRule (deontic conclusion) or deo:ConstitutiveRule (factual conclusion: definitions, counts-as). A rule with no condition holds unconditionally. Corresponds to a ruleml:Rule inside a LegalRuleML PrescriptiveStatement or ConstitutiveStatement, to an ODRL Rule (odrl:Permission, odrl:Prohibition, odrl:Duty) together with its constraints, and to a HydraDL Rule. Link the rule to what it formalises with deo:formalizes.
ex:r_pay_claim
  a deo:PrescriptiveRule ;
  deo:strength deo:DefeasibleStrength ;
  deo:hasCondition ex:c_payable , ex:c_approved_at ;
  deo:activatedBy ex:c_approved_at ;
  deo:hasConsequent ex:chain_pay ;
  deo:formalizes ex:Oblig_Clause8 .

deo:SequencedOperand

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#SequencedOperand
LabelSequenced Operand
Subclass of—
DefinitionAn operand of an and-in-sequence condition, with its position in the sequence.
ex:seq_1
  a deo:SequencedOperand ;
  deo:position 1 ;
  deo:operandCondition ex:c_registered .

deo:SetOperator

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#SetOperator
LabelSet Operator
Subclass of—
DefinitionA comparison operator over classes, parts and sets, for comparison conditions whose operands are not ordered values.
UsageUse the six individuals below. Order comparisons (=, ≠, <, ≤, >, ≥) use the LDSO-Operations comparators instead.
ex:c_eu a deo:ComparisonCondition ; deo:operator deo:IsPartOf .

deo:TemporalCharacteristic

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#TemporalCharacteristic
LabelTemporal Characteristic
Subclass of—
DefinitionA dated change in a rule's legal status: the moment it starts or ends being in force, efficacious, applicable or enforceable.
UsageLegalRuleML TemporalCharacteristic (forStatus, hasStatusDevelopment, atTime). Complements LDSO-Lifecycle (life:validFrom / life:validTo on the source provision): use this when the formalised rule's own validity differs from its provision's, or for statuses other than being in force. Rule validity windows are not yet evaluated by HydraDL.
ex:tc_r1_start
  a deo:TemporalCharacteristic ;
  deo:forStatus deo:StatusInForce ;
  deo:statusDevelopment deo:Starts ;
  deo:atTime "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"^^xsd:dateTime .

deo:Variable

IRIhttps://w3id.org/ldso/deontic#Variable
LabelVariable
Subclass of—
DefinitionA placeholder in a rule, standing for any individual or value; the same variable in several literals of one rule stands for the same individual or value.
UsageVariables are scoped to the rule that uses them. Every variable of a rule must occur in a positive fact, class or property condition of that rule, or be bound by an assignment or an aggregate (rule safety): a reasoner applies rules to the named individuals and computed values only. HydraDL: Term::Variable.
ex:var_claim
  a deo:Variable ;
  rdfs:label "?claim" .

Concept Schemes

deo:AggregateOperatorScheme — Aggregate operators

How an aggregate condition combines the values of its pattern's solutions.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:CountcountThe number of distinct solutions; 0 over none.
HydraDL AggregateOp::Count.
deo:MaxmaximumThe greatest of the solutions' values; none over no solution.
HydraDL AggregateOp::Max.
deo:MinminimumThe least of the solutions' values; none over no solution.
HydraDL AggregateOp::Min.
deo:SumsumThe sum of the solutions' values; 0 over no solution.
HydraDL AggregateOp::Sum.

deo:ConflictStrategyScheme — Conflict strategies

What an evaluation answers when two applicable rules conflict and no override decides between them.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:AmbiguityBlockingambiguity blockingNeither conclusion is drawn; the conflict is reported and the answer is undetermined.
The default of defeasible logic and of HydraDL.
deo:InvalidateinvalidateA conflict makes the whole normative system void.
ODRL conflict invalid (ODRL's default). An evaluation that reports any unresolved conflict answers that the system is void.
deo:PermissionPrevailspermission prevailsA permission prevails over a contrary prohibition.
ODRL conflict perm. Compiles to an override (basis deo:ConflictStrategyBasis) of every permission rule over every contrary prohibition rule.
deo:ProhibitionPrevailsprohibition prevailsA prohibition prevails over a contrary permission.
ODRL conflict prohibit. Compiles to overrides the other way round.

deo:LegalStatusScheme — Legal statuses of rules

Legal statuses a rule can have over time.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:StatusApplicableapplicableThe rule applies to facts occurring in the period.
deo:StatusEfficaciousefficaciousThe rule can produce legal effects.
deo:StatusEnforceableenforceableThe rule's effects can be enforced.
deo:StatusInForcein forceThe rule belongs to the legal system.

deo:LogicalOperatorScheme — Logical operators

How a logical condition combines its operands.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:AndandEvery operand holds.
ODRL odrl:and.
deo:AndSequenceand in sequenceEvery operand holds, one after another in the stated order.
ODRL odrl:andSequence. Not yet executable by HydraDL.
deo:OrorAt least one operand holds.
ODRL odrl:or.
deo:Xoneexactly oneExactly one operand holds.
ODRL odrl:xone.

deo:NormStateScheme — Norm states

Normative states of a deontic statement that a condition can test.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:FulfilledfulfilledThe obligation was complied with, or the prohibition's period ended without infringement.
LegalRuleML Compliance; ODRL fulfilled. HydraDL Condition::Fulfilled.
deo:InForcein forceThe deontic statement is concluded (holds) in the situation.
deo:ViolatedviolatedThe obligation was not complied with by its deadline, or the prohibition was infringed.
LegalRuleML Violation; ODRL infringed (prohibitions) and not fulfilled (duties).

deo:ObligationTypeScheme — Obligation types

Kinds of obligation by what counts as complying with them over time.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:Achievementachievement obligationComplied with when the action is performed at least once within the obligation's period (from activation to deadline).
The default. The only obligation type HydraDL v1 evaluates.
deo:Maintenancemaintenance obligationComplied with only if the state holds at every moment of the obligation's period; violated at the first moment it does not.
Not yet evaluated by HydraDL (v1 non-goal).
deo:Punctualpunctual obligationComplied with only if the action is performed at the very moment the obligation is in force.
Not yet evaluated by HydraDL.

deo:OperationScheme — Operations

The operations an expression applies to its operands.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:Absabsolute valueThe magnitude of the operand.
HydraDL Expr::Abs.
deo:AddsumThe first operand plus the second; an instant plus a duration is an instant.
HydraDL Expr::Add.
deo:AddDaysadd daysThe first operand, an instant, plus a whole number of days (the second).
HydraDL Expr::AddDays.
deo:AddMonthsadd monthsThe first operand, an instant, plus a whole number of calendar months (the second).
HydraDL Expr::AddMonths.
deo:AddYearsadd yearsThe first operand, an instant, plus a whole number of calendar years (the second).
HydraDL Expr::AddYears.
deo:CeilceilingThe least integer not below the operand.
HydraDL Expr::Ceil.
deo:DaysBetweendays betweenWhole civil days from the first instant to the second.
HydraDL Expr::DaysBetween.
deo:DivquotientThe first operand divided by the second, exactly.
HydraDL Expr::Div. Division by zero has no value: a comparison over it is undetermined.
deo:FloorfloorThe greatest integer not above the operand.
HydraDL Expr::Floor.
deo:GreatergreaterThe greater of the two operands, as in max(income − deduction, 0).
HydraDL Expr::Max. For the greatest value over many records, use a deo:AggregateCondition with deo:Max.
deo:LesserlesserThe lesser of the two operands.
HydraDL Expr::Min. For the least value over many records, use a deo:AggregateCondition with deo:Min.
deo:MonthsBetweenmonths betweenWhole calendar months from the first instant to the second.
HydraDL Expr::MonthsBetween.
deo:MulproductThe first operand times the second.
HydraDL Expr::Mul.
deo:NegnegationThe opposite of the operand.
HydraDL Expr::Neg.
deo:NownowThe instant of the evaluation. No operand.
HydraDL Expr::Now.
deo:RoundroundThe operand rounded to deo:places decimal places by deo:roundingMode.
HydraDL Expr::Round(expr, places, Rounding).
deo:SubdifferenceThe first operand minus the second; two instants give a duration.
HydraDL Expr::Sub.
deo:YearsBetweenyears betweenWhole calendar years from the first instant to the second, such as an age.
HydraDL Expr::YearsBetween.

deo:OverrideBasisScheme — Override bases

The legal ground on which one rule prevails over another.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:ConflictStrategyBasisconflict strategyThe override follows from the normative system's declared conflict strategy (ODRL perm or prohibit), not from a specific provision.
deo:ExplicitClauseexplicit clauseA provision states the priority itself ("notwithstanding Article 5", "subject to Section 2").
Cite the provision with deo:basisProvision; LDSO-Semantics may annotate it.
deo:LexPosteriorlex posteriorThe later rule prevails over the earlier one of the same rank.
deo:LexSpecialislex specialisThe more specific rule prevails over the more general one.
deo:LexSuperiorlex superiorThe rule from the higher-ranked source prevails.

deo:PolicyTypeScheme — Policy types

The kind of instrument a normative system is, as ODRL distinguishes them.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:AgreementagreementRules agreed between an assigner and an assignee, in force between them.
ODRL odrl:Agreement. Contracts and insurance policies are agreements.
deo:AssertionassertionA party's statement of the rules it understands to hold.
ODRL Common Vocabulary odrl:Assertion. Evaluated as a set; it records a claim, not an agreement.
deo:OfferofferRules proposed by an assigner; they grant and impose nothing until accepted.
ODRL odrl:Offer. An evaluation treats its rules as not in force.
deo:PrivacyprivacyAn agreement on the processing of personal data, stating the obligations of the data user.
ODRL Common Vocabulary odrl:Privacy. Evaluated as an agreement.
deo:RequestrequestRules an assignee asks to be granted; nothing is in force until granted.
ODRL Common Vocabulary odrl:Request. Evaluated like an offer: its rules are not in force.
deo:SetsetA generic set of rules, in force as stated.
ODRL odrl:Set (the default policy type). Statutes and regulations are sets.
deo:TicketticketRules granted to whoever holds the ticket, the assignee left open.
ODRL Common Vocabulary odrl:Ticket. Evaluated as an agreement whose bearer is a variable bound by a holder condition.

deo:ReparationKindScheme — Reparation kinds

What a stated reparation is, by the kind of norm it answers.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:ConsequenceconsequenceA further duty imposed when a duty is not fulfilled.
ODRL odrl:consequence.
deo:PenaltypenaltyA sanction or correction imposed for a violation.
LegalRuleML PenaltyStatement.
deo:RemedyremedyA duty imposed when a prohibition is infringed.
ODRL odrl:remedy. A remedy cannot itself carry a consequence in ODRL.

deo:RoundingModeScheme — Rounding modes

How deo:Round resolves the digits it drops.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:DowndownToward zero: the dropped digits are discarded.
HydraDL Rounding::Down.
deo:HalfEvenhalf evenTo the nearest neighbour; a tie goes to the even neighbour (banker's rounding).
HydraDL Rounding::HalfEven.
deo:HalfUphalf upTo the nearest neighbour; a tie goes away from zero.
HydraDL Rounding::HalfUp.
deo:UpupAway from zero whenever a nonzero digit is dropped.
HydraDL Rounding::Up.

deo:StatusDevelopmentScheme — Status developments

Whether a legal status starts or ends.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:EndsendsThe status ends at the given time.
deo:StartsstartsThe status begins at the given time.

deo:StrengthScheme — Rule strengths

How a rule's conclusion resists contrary rules.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:DefeasibleStrengthdefeasibleThe conclusion holds when the antecedent holds and no applicable contrary rule prevails over it.
LegalRuleML DefeasibleStrength. HydraDL RuleKind::Defeasible. The default for legal rules with exceptions.
deo:DefeaterStrengthdefeaterThe rule only blocks the contrary conclusion; it never establishes its own conclusion. The typical form of an exception that suspends a norm without imposing the opposite.
LegalRuleML Defeater. HydraDL RuleKind::Defeater.
deo:StrictStrengthstrictThe conclusion holds whenever the antecedent holds indisputably; no contrary rule defeats it.
LegalRuleML StrictStrength. HydraDL RuleKind::Strict. In HydraDL a strict deontic rule is an ordinary supporter that a superior rule can still beat; only factual conclusions have a strict tier.

deo:ValueTypeScheme — Value types

The types an argument of a predicate signature can hold.

ConceptLabelDefinition
deo:DurationdurationA fixed length of time.
HydraDL ValueType::Duration (seconds). Written as xsd:duration in weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds; calendar months and years vary in length and are counted with calendar operations instead.
deo:IndividualindividualA named individual of the ontology: a party, a claim, a dataset.
HydraDL ValueType::Individual. Key arguments are usually individuals.
deo:InstantinstantA point in time, such as a date of birth or the day a claim was filed.
HydraDL ValueType::Instant (seconds). Written as xsd:dateTime.
deo:NumbernumberAn exact rational number: an amount, a rate, a count.
HydraDL ValueType::Number. There is no floating point: 1 ÷ 3 is exactly one third, and rounding happens only where an expression says so. Written as xsd:decimal or xsd:integer.
deo:TexttextA string, such as a code or a category name.
HydraDL ValueType::Text. Texts are only equal or not; they have no order.

deo:SetOperator individuals

IndividualLabelDefinition
deo:HasParthas partThe left operand contains the right operand.
deo:IsAis aThe left operand is an instance of the right operand class.
deo:IsAllOfis all ofThe left operand is every member of the right operand set.
deo:IsAnyOfis any ofThe left operand is a member of the right operand set.
deo:IsNoneOfis none ofThe left operand is no member of the right operand set.
deo:IsPartOfis part ofThe left operand is contained in the right operand.

Object Properties

PropertyDomainRangeCharacteristicsDefinition
deo:aboutStatementdeo:NormConditiondeo:DeonticStatementFunctionalPropertyThe deontic statement whose state a norm condition tests.
deo:actiondeo:DeonticStatementdeo:ActionFunctionalPropertyWhat the statement requires, forbids or permits.
ODRL odrl:action.
deo:activatedBydeo:Ruledeo:FactConditionFunctionalPropertyThe fact condition of the rule whose time sets when the rule's obligation starts (and so when a relative deadline runs from).
Must be one of the rule's own conditions. Absent: the latest time among the rule's timestamped fact conditions. HydraDL: Rule.activated_by. The LDSO-Operations trigger of an operative rule usually corresponds to it.
deo:adopteddeo:Alternativesdeo:RuleFunctionalPropertyThe alternative in use; it must be one of the set's alternatives.
deo:aggregateOperatordeo:AggregateConditionskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertySum, count, minimum or maximum (a concept of deo:AggregateOperatorScheme).
Exactly one per aggregate condition. HydraDL: AggregateOp.
deo:alternativedeo:Alternativesdeo:Rule—One of the mutually exclusive formalisations.
LegalRuleML hasAlternative.
deo:argumentValuedeo:Argument—FunctionalPropertyThe value of the argument: a named entity, an individual IRI, or a deo:Variable.
deo:assertsdeo:FactualStatementdeo:LiteralFunctionalPropertyThe fact a factual statement asserts.
deo:assignee——⊑ deo:bearerThe party a rule is granted or issued to.
ODRL odrl:assignee.
deo:assigner——⊑ deo:auxiliaryPartyThe party that issues the rule.
ODRL odrl:assigner.
deo:assigns——FunctionalPropertyThe fresh variable an assignment or aggregate condition binds.
On a deo:AssignmentCondition or a deo:AggregateCondition; the value is a deo:Variable (left without an rdfs:range so that the shapes can tell an individual from a variable).
deo:authority—ent:NamedEntity—The person or organisation that creates, endorses or enforces the norms.
LegalRuleML Authority. On a normative system or a rule.
deo:auxiliaryPartydeo:DeonticStatement——A party involved in the statement other than its bearer, such as its beneficiary or issuer.
LegalRuleML AuxiliaryParty; parent of deo:assigner and deo:beneficiary.
deo:basisProvisiondeo:Overrideldso:LegalElement—The provision that states or justifies the override.
deo:bearerdeo:DeonticStatement——The party the statement is primarily directed at: who must, must not or may act. A role, a named party, a party collection, or a variable.
LegalRuleML Bearer; ODRL assignee (for a duty's or permission's party). HydraDL: the bearer of O/F/P.
deo:beneficiary——⊑ deo:auxiliaryPartyThe party in whose favour the statement holds (the creditor of an obligation).
deo:classExpressiondeo:ClassCondition—FunctionalPropertyThe OWL class (named, or a class expression node) the subject must belong to.
deo:concludesdeo:ConstitutiveRuledeo:LiteralFunctionalPropertyThe factual conclusion of a constitutive rule.
deo:conflictStrategydeo:NormativeSystemskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertyWhat an unresolved conflict yields (a concept of deo:ConflictStrategyScheme).
ODRL odrl:conflict. Absent: ambiguity blocking.
deo:correlativedeo:Rightdeo:DeonticStatement—An obligation or prohibition on an auxiliary party that a right implies.
Compare LDSO-Semantics leg:correlatesTo, which annotates the same relation in text.
deo:deadlinedeo:DeonticStatementops:ScheduleFunctionalPropertyWhen the statement must be complied with: by an absolute date (ops:deadlineDate), within a duration from activation (ops:deadlineDuration), or on a recurring schedule.
Reuses the LDSO-Operations schedules. An ops:Deadline gives one due time: HydraDL Deadline::At for a date, Deadline::Within for a duration counted from activation. No deadline: the obligation must be met by the time of evaluation. An ops:RecurringSchedule or ops:PeriodSchedule states a recurring obligation (pay every month); HydraDL does not yet evaluate those.
deo:declaresCompletedeo:NormativeSystem——A predicate, class or property whose record is complete: an unrecorded fact of it counts as false rather than unknown.
The closed-world declaration. Without it every record is open, and the absence of a record (for example of a payment) never proves that something did not happen. HydraDL: NormSystem.closed. Only predicates that no rule concludes may be declared complete.
deo:declaresSignaturedeo:NormativeSystemdeo:PredicateSignature—The signature of a predicate that carries values in this normative system.
At most one signature per predicate, including those of the systems inherited from. HydraDL: NormSystem.signatures.
deo:deonticContentdeo:DeonticStatementdeo:DeonticStatementFunctionalPropertyThe deontic statement this one is about, in place of an action: an obligation to grant a permission, a permission to impose an obligation.
LegalRuleML deontic elements are recursive (an Obligation may contain a Permission). A statement has either a deo:action or a deo:deonticContent. The common case — an obligation to let someone act — is usually better stated as a deo:Right with its correlative. Not evaluated by HydraDL, whose norms are over actions.
deo:formalizes———What a formal term formalises: the LDSO-Semantics annotation (normative statement, condition, exception, definition) or the LDSO-Operations operative rule it is the formal counterpart of.
The provenance link from the formal layer to the annotated text. A reasoner's explanation cites the source provision through it: deo:formalizes → leg:annotates → the structural element and its citation. Domain: a rule, a condition or a deontic statement.
deo:forStatusdeo:TemporalCharacteristicskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertyThe legal status that changes (a concept of deo:LegalStatusScheme).
LegalRuleML forStatus.
deo:fulfilmentComparatordeo:DeonticStatementops:ComparatorFunctionalPropertyHow a recorded action's value must compare with the value the statement requires, read "recorded comparator required": an obligation to pay at least the fee is fulfilled by a payment ≥ the fee.
Absent: ops:Equal. Anything else needs an action whose predicate has a signature with exactly one value argument after its key (an ordered one, not a text, for <, ≤, >, ≥). One payment is compared at a time: partial payments are not summed. ODRL: a duty refined by a payAmount constraint. HydraDL: Deontic.fulfilment (fulfilled_when).
deo:hasAlternativesdeo:NormativeSystemdeo:Alternatives—A set of alternative formalisations within the normative system.
deo:hasArgumentdeo:Literaldeo:Argument—One argument of the literal.
deo:hasArgumentSlotdeo:PredicateSignaturedeo:ArgumentSlot—One argument position of the signature.
One slot per argument, indexed 0..n-1 by deo:argumentIndex; a literal of the predicate has as many arguments as the signature has slots. HydraDL: Signature.args, in index order.
deo:hasChainElementdeo:ReparationChaindeo:ChainElement—A position of the reparation chain.
deo:hasConditiondeo:Ruledeo:Condition—One conjunct of the rule's antecedent.
ruleml:if; ODRL odrl:constraint. All conditions of a rule must hold for it to apply.
deo:hasConsequentdeo:PrescriptiveRule—FunctionalPropertyThe deontic conclusion of a prescriptive rule: a deontic statement or a reparation chain.
ruleml:then (a SuborderList in LegalRuleML).
deo:hasFactualStatementdeo:NormativeSystemdeo:FactualStatement—A factual statement the normative system makes.
deo:hasOperanddeo:Expressiondeo:ExpressionOperand—One operand of the expression.
Distinct from deo:operand, which gives the operands of a logical condition.
deo:hasOverridedeo:NormativeSystemdeo:Override—An override that holds within the normative system.
LegalRuleML OverrideStatement / hasQualification.
deo:hasReparationdeo:NormativeSystemdeo:Reparation—A reparation stated within the normative system.
LegalRuleML ReparationStatement.
deo:hasRuledeo:NormativeSystemdeo:Rule—A rule of the normative system.
ODRL odrl:permission / odrl:prohibition / odrl:obligation; LegalRuleML hasStatement.
deo:implies———Between act types: when the first is exercised, the second is not prohibited.
ODRL odrl:implies. Compiles to a defeater against prohibitions of the second act whenever the first is permitted and exercised.
deo:imposesdeo:Reparation—FunctionalPropertyWhat the violation imposes: a deontic statement or a reparation chain.
LegalRuleML appliesPenalty; ODRL consequence / remedy value.
deo:includedIn——TransitivePropertyBetween act types: performing the first counts as performing the second.
ODRL odrl:includedIn. Compiles to strict constitutive rules (doing the narrower act is doing the broader one).
deo:inheritsFromdeo:NormativeSystemdeo:NormativeSystemTransitivePropertyA normative system whose rules this one includes.
ODRL odrl:inheritFrom.
deo:jurisdiction—ent:NamedEntity—The territory or subject matter over which the norms apply.
LegalRuleML Jurisdiction. On a normative system or a rule.
deo:leftOperanddeo:ComparisonCondition—FunctionalPropertyWhat is compared: an ODRL left operand (dateTime, count, spatial…) or a domain measure.
ODRL odrl:leftOperand.
deo:legalSource—ldso:LegalResource—The legal instrument the norms derive from.
LegalRuleML LegalSource / fromLegalSources. On a normative system, a rule or an Alternatives set.
deo:logicalOperatordeo:LogicalConditionskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertyAnd, or, exactly one, or and-in-sequence (a concept of deo:LogicalOperatorScheme).
deo:memberOf—deo:Collection—A collection the resource belongs to.
ODRL odrl:partOf.
deo:normStatedeo:NormConditionskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertyThe state tested (a concept of deo:NormStateScheme).
deo:objectdeo:PropertyCondition—FunctionalPropertyThe second individual or variable of a property condition.
deo:obligationTypedeo:DeonticStatementskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertyAchievement, maintenance or punctual (a concept of deo:ObligationTypeScheme).
Absent: achievement. Applies to obligations and prohibitions (a prohibition is a maintenance obligation of the negated action over its period).
deo:operanddeo:LogicalCondition——An operand of a logical condition: a condition, or a sequenced operand for and-in-sequence.
deo:operandConditiondeo:SequencedOperanddeo:ConditionFunctionalPropertyThe condition at a position of an and-in-sequence.
deo:operationdeo:Expressionskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertyThe operation an expression applies (a concept of deo:OperationScheme).
Exactly one per expression; it fixes the number of operands. HydraDL: the Expr variant.
deo:operatordeo:ComparisonCondition—FunctionalPropertyThe comparison: an ops:Comparator or a deo:SetOperator.
ODRL odrl:operator.
deo:overriddendeo:Overridedeo:RuleFunctionalPropertyThe rule that yields.
LegalRuleML Override @under.
deo:overrideBasisdeo:Overrideskos:Concept—The legal ground of the override (a concept of deo:OverrideBasisScheme).
deo:overridingdeo:Overridedeo:RuleFunctionalPropertyThe rule that prevails.
LegalRuleML Override @over.
deo:patterndeo:AggregateConditiondeo:Condition—One condition of the pattern an aggregate ranges over: a fact, class or property condition.
All the pattern's conditions must hold together for a solution.
deo:policyTypedeo:NormativeSystemskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertyThe kind of instrument (a concept of deo:PolicyTypeScheme).
deo:predicatedeo:Literal—FunctionalPropertyThe predicate of the literal: the IRI of a relation, an act type or a concept.
deo:propertydeo:PropertyConditionowl:ObjectPropertyFunctionalPropertyThe OWL object property the subject and object must stand in.
deo:refinement—deo:Condition—A condition narrowing an action, an asset collection or a party collection.
ODRL odrl:refinement. A compiler adds it to the conditions of each rule that uses the refined term.
deo:repairsdeo:Reparationdeo:DeonticStatementFunctionalPropertyThe statement whose violation the reparation answers.

deo:reparationKinddeo:Reparationskos:ConceptFunctionalPropertyConsequence, remedy or penalty (a concept of deo:ReparationKindScheme).

deo:rightOperandReferencedeo:ComparisonCondition—FunctionalPropertyA resource whose value is the right operand, to be looked up when evaluating.

Datatype Properties

PropertyDomainRangeCharacteristicsDefinition
deo:argumentIndex—xsd:integerFunctionalPropertyThe 0-based position of an argument in its literal, or of an argument slot in its signature.
On a deo:Argument or a deo:ArgumentSlot.
deo:atTimedeo:TemporalCharacteristicxsd:dateTimeFunctionalPropertyWhen the status development occurs.
LegalRuleML atTime.
deo:dataTypedeo:ComparisonConditionxsd:anyURIFunctionalPropertyThe datatype of the right operand.
ODRL odrl:dataType.
deo:isQuantitydeo:PredicateSignaturexsd:booleanFunctionalPropertyTrue for a quantity, which has one value per key; false for a relation, which may have any number.
A quantity is never negated in a rule: "the value is not 100" is a comparison, and a defeater blocks a value without giving another. HydraDL: Signature.quantity.
deo:keyLengthdeo:PredicateSignaturexsd:integerFunctionalPropertyThe number of leading arguments of the predicate that identify a record.
At most the number of argument slots. A quantity has exactly one slot after its key. HydraDL: Signature.key.
deo:negated—xsd:booleanFunctionalPropertyWhether the literal or condition is negated. Absent: false.
On a literal (including actions and fact conditions), a class, property or norm condition.
deo:paraphrase—rdf:langString—A natural-language rendering of a formal rule, for review.
LegalRuleML Paraphrase. Useful to check an LLM-proposed formalisation against its source text.
deo:perdurantdeo:DeonticStatementxsd:booleanFunctionalPropertyWhether the obligation remains in force after it has been violated (paying late still owes the payment). Absent: false.
HydraDL evaluates non-perdurant obligations only; the violation stays on record either way.
